Slotted ALOHA.example: At G=1, S=e⁻¹≈0.368 successful frames per frame time.

symbols: bits that fit in the link during one propagation delay
fraction of time spent transmitting useful data
round-trip time excluding the stated frame transmission time
Stop-and-Wait utilization.example: At Ttx=2 ms and RTT=8 ms, U=20%, ignoring ACK transmission time.

symbols: address count including network and broadcast where applicable
IPv4 addresses per block.example: A /26 leaves 6 host bits and has 2⁶=64 addresses.

symbols: total addresses required including reserved addresses as applicable
VLSM prefix selection.example: For 50 ordinary hosts, 52 addresses are needed. h=6 gives 64 addresses and a /26.

symbols: byte position in the original IP payload
IPv4 fragment offset.example: If the fragment starts 1,480 bytes into the payload, its offset is 185.

TCP window limit.example: cwnd=12,000 bytes and rwnd=8,000 bytes cap outstanding data at 8,000 bytes.

symbols: estimated least cost to the destination
Distance vector.example: A link to B costing 2 plus B’s reported cost 3 to D yields a candidate cost 5 from A to D.

symbols: settled or source-side vertex for this relaxation
Dijkstra relaxation.example: If d(v)=9, d(u)=4 and w(u,v)=3, replace d(v) with 7.

Hamming redundancy.example: For m=7, r=4 satisfies 16≥12, while r=3 fails 8≥11.

symbols: data bits with the CRC remainder appended
remainder from modulo-2 division after appending zeros
CRC / XOR division.example: Data 1101 with generator 101 produces remainder 10, so the transmitted codeword is 110110.

symbols: idealized upper bound on delivered data rate
TCP throughput bound.example: An 80,000-bit window and 20 ms RTT cap throughput at 4 Mb/s on a 10 Mb/s bottleneck.

Pure ALOHA.example: At G=0.5, S=0.5e⁻¹≈0.184 successful frames per frame time.

symbols: minimum frame length for collision detection
CSMA/CD minimum frame.example: At d=500 m, v=2×10⁸ m/s, R=100 Mb/s, the propagation lower bound is 500 bits.

symbols: total bytes on the accounting basis used
Ethernet payload rate.example: At R=100 Mb/s, payload/total=1500/1538 and η=0.9, useful rate is about 87.8 Mb/s.

Transmission & propagation delay.example: 8,000 bits at 1 Mb/s take 8 ms to transmit. A 400 km path at 2×10⁸ m/s adds 2 ms propagation.

symbols: outstanding TCP data needed to fill the pipe
TCP window for RTT.example: At 20 Mb/s and RTT=40 ms, W≈800,000 bits or 100,000 bytes.

Ethernet minimum data.example: A 64-byte frame with 18 bytes of Ethernet header and trailer needs at least 46 bytes in its data field, padding if necessary.

symbols: number of embedded objects after the base page
Persistent HTTP timing.example: Three objects take about 5 RTTs on one fresh persistent connection without pipelining, ignoring DNS and transmission time.

symbols: new contiguous bytes acknowledged relative to SEQ
TCP sequence and acknowledgment.example: With SEQ=1000 and ACK=1460, 460 bytes were acknowledged, ignoring wraparound and SYN/FIN.

symbols: round down to a whole number
Full MSS segments in a window.example: W=5,000 bytes and MSS=1,460 bytes fit 3 full segments.

symbols: whole RTT rounds required to reach the target in ideal slow start
Slow-start rounds to a target.example: Starting at 1 MSS, a 10-MSS target requires 4 rounds. At 25 ms per RTT that is 100 ms.

symbols: phase with approximate doubling each RTT
AIMD and timeout.example: A cwnd of 4 MSS becomes about 8 MSS in a slow-start RTT, versus 5 MSS in an avoidance RTT.

symbols: number of equal subnets, a power of two
Equal-size subnet split.example: Splitting a /24 into 8 equal subnets adds 3 bits and gives /27.

symbols: highest address in an ordinary broadcast subnet
Network and broadcast addresses.example: For 192.168.1.70/26, network is .64 and broadcast is .127.

symbols: extra bits, so the share is one over 2 to the k
CIDR allocation by fraction.example: A 1/8 share of a /21 adds k=3, giving /24.

symbols: length of IPv4 header and data
IPv4 IHL and data length.example: IHL=6 and Total Length=500 give H=24 and payload 476 bytes.

symbols: maximum whole IP datagram on the outgoing link
Aligned fragment payload.example: With MTU=1,500 and H=24, use 1,472 bytes for each full nonfinal fragment.

symbols: file data being divided directly into IP payloads
Datagrams needed for a file.example: For F=3,000, MTU=1,500 and H=20, N=3 and last payload=40 bytes.

symbols: application bytes in the TCP segment
Maximum TCP payload over IPv4.example: With 20-byte IP and TCP headers, the IPv4 length field limits the TCP payload to 65,495 bytes.

symbols: maximum sender window for the named ARQ protocol
ARQ sequence space and windows.example: At m=3 there are 8 sequence numbers. Go-Back-N allows a sender window up to 7, Selective Repeat up to 4.

symbols: node processing, queue, or total delay as subscripted
Nodal delay and bottleneck rate.example: Delays of 1, 2, 3 and 4 ms total 10 ms. Rates 10, 5 and 20 Mb/s give a 5 Mb/s path bottleneck.

symbols: time to serve a caravan at the booth and propagate to the next point
Caravan and toll-booth delay.example: Ten cars at 12 s each plus 60 km at 100 km/h take 2+36=38 minutes.

symbols: bits simultaneously present on the link
Bits in flight and physical bit length.example: At 1 Mb/s and 2×10⁸ m/s, each bit spans 200 m and a 20 km link holds up to 100 bits in flight.

symbols: fraction of transmitted bytes used by headers
Encapsulation overhead.example: Four 20-byte headers on a 1,000-byte message use 80/1,080≈7.4% of transmitted bytes.

symbols: TCP connections needed, one per object
time with sequential connections, ignoring transfer time
Nonpersistent HTTP connections and time.example: Four objects at RTT=30 ms use four connections and about 240 ms of serial RTT overhead.

symbols: data bit at a given position
Single and two-dimensional parity.example: Data 1011 has even parity bit 1. A 3×4 layout uses 7 row and column parity bits, plus a corner bit if the scheme includes one.

symbols: add carry bits back into the low end
Internet checksum.example: Adding 0xFFFF and 0x0001 folds to 0x0001. Its complement is 0xFFFE.

ALOHA successful frames and bit rate.example: With S=0.25 and 2 ms frames, 125 frames/s succeed. At 1 Mb/s, that is 250 kb/s.

symbols: collision count for the current frame
Ethernet binary exponential backoff.example: At n=3, choose K from 0 through 7. K=4 at 51.2 μs per slot gives 204.8 μs.
